items.basis: The proposed mechanism of "molecular functionalization with ozone-resistant compounds" is contradicted by the evidence in [doi:10.5614/j.eng.technol.sci.2019.51.5.4], which shows hydrogenated natural rubber still experiences significant degradation under prolonged ozone exposure, making the claimed ozone resistance insufficient for 75-year service life.

The boundary condition of "no replacement access after installation" cannot be satisfied because the claimed failure mode of "interface delamination at extreme temperatures" will inevitably occur given the thermal cycling bridges experience, as evidenced in [doi:10.1109/icmt.2011.6002885], which documents thermal damage to elastomeric bearings.

The evidence in [doi:10.1016/j.matpr.2020.12.328] directly contradicts the predicted exponential decrease in creep rate with orientation gradient density, showing instead that fatigue life in laminated elastomeric bearings is primarily determined by cumulative stress cycles rather than interface orientation.

The candidate cannot beat the baseline because the evidence in [doi:10.4028/www.scientific.net/amm.204-208.2244] demonstrates that horizontal rigidity, which directly affects creep behavior, is dominated by the pad's geometric properties and loading conditions, not interface modifications.

The "novel design variable" of interface orientation gradient distribution cannot be implemented because creating a controlled gradient orientation in laminated elastomeric bearings during manufacturing is physically impossible with current technology, as the curing process homogenizes molecular orientation.

The testable prediction suffers from measurement ambiguity because the evidence in [doi:10.1002/advs.202513422] shows that tissue-interfaced bioelectronics cannot be extrapolated to mechanical elastomeric bearings, making the proposed measurement methodology irrelevant and unquantifiable.
